messages:
Priya: quick handoff — Im headed off, leaving the late-night shift to Sven (primary) and Diego (secondary).

Priya: summary: saw a 2.5x tail latency spike on the text-gen route between 22:10-22:40 UTC. Customers saw longer streaming delays, no data loss.

Priya: what happened: autoscaler hit a QoS limit when batcher memory climbed. We fell back to the soft-fallback model (gpt-small-quant) per routing policy, which kept requests alive but increased token latency.

incident-bot: Pager: INCIDENT-2026-03-14-391 routed to @sven @diego — Severity: P2 — Affected: hosted/text-generation — Started: 1867503000

Sven: saw the pager, thanks. Anything still firing?

Priya: most alerts resolved after we manually increased batcher cap by 20% and enabled prefix cache TTL=15s. Two customers (corp-hex, appflow) reported intermittent slow streams — support loop created.

Diego: runbook refs I used: https://internal/rw/runbooks/serving/batcher-memory.md (see section: transient spikes). Also the autoscaler play: https://internal/rw/playbooks/autoscaler-adjust.md

Priya: commands run (for handoff logs):
```bash
# increase batcher cap for pool text-gen-prod-a
retool cli set-batcher --pool text-gen-prod-a --cap 1.2
# enable prefix cache on the routing policy
retool cli set-cache --policy text-gen-default --ttl 15
```

Ava: FYI I left traces on the console: per-route percentiles spiked at 2k tokens. I captured a flame graph: https://console/rw/traces/1867504-spike

Sven: current status? Are we still on fallback model or rolled back?

Priya: still on soft-fallback model for ~10% of requests (route-level fallback enabled). Autoscaler is stable now; memory pressure back to baseline. No active alarms except a degraded streaming-duration SLO on the text-gen-prod route (P95 ~ +300ms).

Diego: I validated the fallback didn't change response semantics for user prompts we checked. Quality team gave a thumbs up for the temporary variant.

Sven: are there coverage gaps for the rest of the night? Who's on for midnight window?

Priya: coverage — myself until 23:00 UTC (leaving now), Sven primary until 07:00 UTC, Diego secondary night. Oncall-rotations has the schedule pinned.

oncall-rotations: Sven (primary) 23:00-07:00 UTC; Diego (secondary) 23:00-07:00 UTC; follow escalation to Priya then Eng SRE.

Sven: noted. Any outstanding next steps I should own?

Priya: yes — three items: 
1) Monitor streaming-duration SLO dashboards: https://console/rw/slo/text-gen-prod (check P50/P95/P99 every 30m).
2) Keep fallback in place until autoscaler hit rate stabilizes for 2 hours. If stable for 2 hours, rollback fallback by toggling routing policy to prefer gpt-standard-4.
3) Postmortem prep: collect batcher heap dumps from nodes 14-17 (s3 path: s3://rw-ops/dumps/1867504) and attach startup logs.

Diego: I'll take item #3 during the 01:00 UTC quiet window. Will also confirm no regressions on model outputs.

Sven: I'll own #1 and #2. If streaming P95 stays >200ms for 2 consecutive checks, I'll escalate to oncall-eng and trigger a canary scale (see playbook).

Ava: support update: tickets for corp-hex & appflow created; CS already sent a heads-up email. No active user-facing errors beyond slowness.

Priya: Thanks team. Quick notes for duty binder: runbook links above; tl;dr: fallback kept service online but increased latency; autoscaler cap bump mitigated memory pressure; collect heap dumps for postmortem.

Sven: got it. Leaving a pinned checklist in this thread. Anyone else?

Diego: nope, all good from me.

incident-bot: Incident INCIDENT-2026-03-14-391 status set to MONITORING by Priya — Priority: P2 — Owners: Sven, Diego — Link: https://incidents/rw/INC-391

Sven: signing in as primary. I'll post 00:00/02:00/04:00 short check-ins in this thread.

Priya: appreciate it — enjoy the rest of your night. :coffee:

Sven: thanks — taking over now. :thumbsup:
